title: The Machine of Sector Nine
premise: Fifteen years after the original Cyrus Okonkwo was murdered aboard a colony freighter, his clone has quietly hauled cargo through the contested orbits of Sector Nine, hiding from a war between the colonial Compact and the orbital Syndicates. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream—a machine buried in the sector's dead station that can broadcast a message no one can ignore—Cyrus discovers the original encoded the proof of his own murder, and the identity of his killer, inside that machine. Hunted by Compact intelligence and the Syndicates alike, Cyrus must choose between delivering a truth that will shatter the fragile peace and protecting the woman who loved the original and now, impossibly, is beginning to love him. In the end, Cyrus broadcasts the message, exposing the Compact admiral who orchestrated the murder, and accepts exile with Mara—no longer a copy, but the last honest man in Sector Nine.
about_author: Oscar Thornbury is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. He lives in a coastal town where he repairs old radios and insists, politely, that he has never been to space.

chapters.title: Deadweight
chapters.summary: Cyrus Okonkwo's POV. Cyrus hauls contraband seed grain through a Syndicate checkpoint, hiding his clone status behind forged papers and a dead man's name. A routine inspection turns dangerous when a scanner flags his genetic profile. Emotional beat: the exhausting cost of being invisible.

chapters.title: The Children's Dream
chapters.summary: POV: Amara, a ten-year-old in the colony's lower habitat. She wakes screaming from a dream of a dark corridor and a door marked with nine scratches—identical to forty other children's dreams. Her teacher logs it, and the report travels upward into dangerous hands. Emotional beat: innocent dread rippling outward.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A Compact intelligence officer named Voss boards Cyrus's ship with a warrant and one question: what did the original Cyrus know? Cyrus claims ignorance, but Voss leaves a tracker. Emotional beat: the past tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: POV: Mara Ilic, the original's former partner, now a station medic. She recognizes Cyrus's gait in a docking bay and confronts him with fifteen years of grief and anger. She has been dreaming too. Emotional beat: love and resentment colliding in one face.

chapters.title: Nine Scratches
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Mara shows him the children's dream maps—every one points to the derelict station Halcyon-9. Cyrus realizes the original hid something there before he died. Emotional beat: the horrifying discovery that his predecessor planned his own posthumous move.

chapters.title: The Tracker
chapters.summary: POV: Voss. The intelligence officer reports to Admiral Kessler that the clone is moving, and is ordered to let him lead them to the machine—then erase everyone involved. Emotional beat: cold institutional arithmetic, a human life weighed against a war.

chapters.title: Running Silent
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus and Mara slip past the blockade using a dead Syndicate courier's codes. In the quiet of the hold, they speak honestly about the original for the first time. Emotional beat: grief becoming intimacy, awkward and real.

chapters.title: Halcyon-9
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Cyrus and Mara. The derelict station is a tomb of frozen crew and failed hydroponics. They follow the children's dream-geometry to a sealed vault behind the reactor. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear—the station remembers its dead.

chapters.title: The Machine
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The vault holds the Loom, an ancient broadcast engine the original helped discover and then hid. A recorded message from the original Cyrus addresses his clone directly: 'You were never supposed to carry this. I'm sorry.' Emotional beat: being spoken to by your own ghost.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. The recording reveals Admiral Kessler ordered the freighter destroyed to bury evidence of Compact war crimes against Syndicate civilians. The original smuggled the proof out before he was caught. Emotional beat: loyalty to the dead man warring with loyalty to the living truth.

chapters.title: Syndicate Waters
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A Syndicate patrol captures them; Cyrus bargains for their lives by offering a fragment of the truth. The Syndicate commander, a former colonist, hesitates—she has dreamed the dream too. Emotional beat: enemies recognizing shared wounds.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. Mara argues the message must go out; Cyrus argues it will ignite a war the colonies can't survive. Their first real fight. Emotional beat: love against duty, both refusing to be wrong.

chapters.title: Kessler's Peace
chapters.summary: POV: Admiral Kessler. The admiral, a genuine believer in order, prepares a preemptive strike on the Syndicate shipyards to force surrender before the truth surfaces. Emotional beat: a villain who thinks she is the last adult in the room.

chapters.title: Amara's Door
chapters.summary: POV: Amara. The children's dreams sharpen—the machine is waking, and it is calling them, not the adults. Amara leads the dreamers to the colony's comms hub, forcing the crisis into the open. Emotional beat: children out-braving their protectors.

chapters.title: Voss Defects
chapters.summary: POV: Voss. Ordered to kill a ship full of civilians, Voss reads the original's evidence fragment and breaks. He sends Cyrus a warning and the strike timetable. Emotional beat: a career loyalist choosing truth over institution at personal ruin.

chapters.title: The Long Orbit
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Racing Kessler's strike clock, Cyrus and Mara plot a broadcast path through the sector's dead relays. The Syndicate commander commits her ships to cover them. Emotional beat: a smuggler becoming, against his will, a courier of history.

chapters.title: Boarding Action
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. Compact marines storm Halcyon-9; Mara holds the vault door with a welding torch and a stolen sidearm while Cyrus splices the Loom into the station grid. She is wounded. Emotional beat: duty and love finally pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. With minutes before Kessler's strike, Cyrus transmits the evidence on every open channel—the war crimes, the murder, the admiral's name. The children, linked through the Loom, carry the signal into every dream on the sector. Emotional beat: the terrible relief of a truth that cannot be taken back.

chapters.title: The War That Didn't Start
chapters.summary: POV: Kessler. The strike fleet receives the broadcast mid-approach. Crews refuse orders; Kessler's command fractures, and she is taken into custody by her own officers. Emotional beat: an empire of silence collapsing in a single hour.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV: Amara. The dreams stop. The children, no longer needed as messengers, grieve the loss of their shared world. Amara meets Cyrus briefly and tells him the machine said thank you. Emotional beat: wonder settling into memory.

chapters.title: What's in a Name
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Offered a hero's place in the new provisional government, Cyrus declines. The original's name belongs to the dead; Cyrus chooses to sign his testimony simply 'Cyrus,' no surname, no lineage. Emotional beat: claiming an identity no one handed him.

chapters.title: Departures
chapters.summary: POV: Mara, closing with Cyrus. Cyrus and Mara take his battered freighter out past the checkpoint lines, exiled by choice, together. Mara asks where they're going; he says somewhere no one has ever dreamed of. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope—the first chapter of a life that is entirely his own.
